name: Leo I
pdTranslations: NPNF translation of sermons and letters available at CCEL (Philip Schaff collection); 19th-century public domain versions widely available.
modernTranslations: Complete modern English translation by Jane Patricia Freeland and Agnes Josephine Conway; also Fathers of the Church series translation.
untranslatedHighlights: Essentially all major works translated; no significant untranslated corpus.

name: Boetius
pdTranslations: H.R. James translation (1897) on Project Gutenberg; Chaucer's medieval translation; King Alfred's paraphrase.
modernTranslations: Multiple modern translations including Victor Watts (Penguin Classics), Richard H. Green (Macmillan Library of Liberal Arts 1962), and others.
untranslatedHighlights: Consolation of Philosophy extensively translated; nearly a dozen major English versions exist.

name: Isidorus Hispalensis
pdTranslations: Partial 19th-century translations available; some sections in public domain.
modernTranslations: Complete modern English translation by Stephen A. Barney, W. J. Lewis, J. A. Beach, and Oliver Berghof (Cambridge University Press, 2010); also Priscilla Throop translation (UNT Digital Library).
untranslatedHighlights: Etymologies (all 20 books) now fully translated; comprehensive coverage achieved.

name: Cassiodorus Vivariensis
pdTranslations: Thomas Hodgkin condensed translation (19th c., Project Gutenberg) of the letters; older partial translations.
modernTranslations: Michael Shane Bjornlie's complete modern English translation of all 468 letters in the Variae (University of California Press); comprehensive modern edition.
untranslatedHighlights: Variae fully translated; Expositio Psalmorum and other works largely untranslated.

name: Petrus Abaelardus
pdTranslations: Older translations of Historia calamitatum and Abelard-Heloise correspondence (19th c.).
modernTranslations: Abelard and Heloise: The Letters and Other Writings (Hackett Classics, tr. Stanley Lombardo and William Levitan); Letters of Peter Abelard, Beyond the Personal (Medieval Texts for Historians, tr. Jan M. Ziolkowski); Penguin Books edition (tr. Elizabeth Radice).
untranslatedHighlights: Major autobiographical works and correspondence fully translated; first complete English translation of all seven letters in modern era.

name: Hildegardis Bingensis
modernTranslations: The Letters of Hildegard of Bingen (3 volumes, Oxford University Press, tr. Joseph L. Baird and Radd K. Ehrman); Hildegard von Bingen's Physica (complete English translation); multiple scholarly translations of Liber divinorum operum and Scivias.
untranslatedHighlights: Letters and major mystical writings translated; some minor devotional texts remain untranslated.

name: Richardus S. Victoris
modernTranslations: Richard of Saint Victor, On the Trinity: English Translation and Commentary (Ruben Angelici, 2011); earlier partial translations by Zinn (1979, book three only) and Cooman (2010); Brepols Library of Christian Sources bilingual edition.
untranslatedHighlights: De Trinitate now fully translated; most other works remain in Latin only.

name: Honorius Augustodunensis
modernTranslations: Imago Mundi (examination and complete text translation); Gemma Animae / Jewel of the Soul (tr. Zachary Thomas and Gerhard Eger); De Neocosmo (with Latin text and English translation); Elucidarium (vernacular translations medieval, modern scholarly translations); Sigillum sanctae Mariae.
untranslatedHighlights: Major works (Imago Mundi, Gemma Animae, Elucidarium) translated; smaller commentaries remain untranslated.

name: Paschasius Radbertus
modernTranslations: De corpore et sanguine Domini with Letter to Fredugard (Corpus Christianorum in Translation series, tr. Mark G. Vaillancourt, Brepols); this is the first monograph on the Eucharist.
untranslatedHighlights: De corpore translated; Mariological treatises and other works untranslated.

name: Hincmarus Rhemensis
modernTranslations: De divortio Lotharii regis et Theutbergae reginae (tr. Rachel Stone and Charles West, Manchester 2016); De ordine palatii (multiple translations); Hincmar of Rheims: On Kingship, Divorce, Virtues and Vices (tr. Priscilla Throop, 2014); draft translations from Collaborative Hincmar Project.
untranslatedHighlights: Several major political and theological treatises remain untranslated; extensive corpus only partially covered.

name: Gratianus
modernTranslations: The Treatise on Laws (Decretum DD. 1-20) with Ordinary Gloss (CUA Press, Studies in Medieval and Early Modern Canon Law); only first twenty distinctions translated.
untranslatedHighlights: Decretum consists of three parts; only the first part (Treatise on Laws) has English translation. The causae and canones remain untranslated.

name: Petrus Damianus
pdTranslations: St Peter Damian: Selected Writings on the Spiritual Life (tr. Patricia McNulty, 1959); Cardinal Petrus Damianus hymn translated by Athanasius Diedrich Wackerbarth.
modernTranslations: Letters 91-120 including De divina omnipotentia (tr. O.J. Blum, FOTC Medieval Continuation 5, 1998); partial translations scattered across academic publications.
untranslatedHighlights: Most of the large letter collection remains untranslated; many theological treatises lack English versions.

name: Hildebertus Cenomanensis
modernTranslations: Some poems translated including 'The Gods Have Faces': Biblical Epigrams and Short Poems; scattered translations in academic articles.
untranslatedHighlights: Most prose works untranslated; sermons and treatises lack English versions. Poems on Rome partially translated.

name: Herveus Burgidolensis
modernTranslations: No English translations found despite extensive searching.
untranslatedHighlights: Entire corpus untranslated. Known for Commentarii in Isaiam prophetam (Isaiah commentary) and other biblical exegesis.

name: Ivo Carnotensis
modernTranslations: No English translations of canonical works (Tripartita, Decretum, Panormia) found; letters extensively studied but not translated.
untranslatedHighlights: All three major canonical collections remain in Latin. 288 letters studied in academic publications but not translated into English.

name: Bruno Carthusianorum
modernTranslations: Mortuary roll of Bruno (complete text in English and German translation, Brepols); no comprehensive translation of theological or spiritual writings.
untranslatedHighlights: Vast majority of writings remain untranslated; only the mortuary roll has English version.

name: Philippus de Harveng
modernTranslations: No English translations found despite extensive searching. Works remain in Latin scholarly literature.
untranslatedHighlights: Entire corpus untranslated. Known works include Responsio de damnatione Salomonis, Life of Augustine of Hippo, and theological writings.

name: Martinus Legionensis
modernTranslations: No English translations found despite extensive searching. Known for Liber Sermonum (Book of Sermons).
untranslatedHighlights: Entire corpus untranslated. Liber Sermonum (c.1200) and biblical commentaries remain in Latin only.

name: Godefridus Admontensis
modernTranslations: Limited translations; Chronicon Gotwicense noted as available in English (1732 publication). Homilies remain largely untranslated.
untranslatedHighlights: Homiliae Dominicales et Festivales (extensive homiletic collection) remain untranslated; vast majority of works in Latin only.

name: Isidorus Mercator
modernTranslations: No English translations found despite extensive searching. The False Decretals remain in Latin scholarly editions.
untranslatedHighlights: Entire Pseudo-Isidorian Decretals collection remains untranslated. Best Latin edition is Hinschius (1863) but no complete English translation exists.
